exposure: Maternal caesarean birth experience (any vs. all vaginal)
cohort: The study included 107 women who provided birth narratives about their own births and those of their maternal relatives, including grandmothers, mothers, sisters, and daughters.
finding: Daughters of mothers who experienced any caesarean birth were significantly more likely to experience caesarean birth themselves compared to daughters of mothers with all vaginal births, indicating a clustering of operative births within family lineages.
mod_finding: Parity was higher for women experiencing all vaginal births compared to those with all caesarean births, but highest for women who experienced any caesarean.
